questions.question: High-speed storage interface connecting SSDs directly to the motherboard.
questions.explanation: NVMe uses PCIe lanes for extremely fast storage access.

questions.question: Chip on the motherboard managing data flow between CPU, memory, and peripherals.
questions.explanation: The chipset determines motherboard capabilities and compatibility.

questions.question: Technology allowing a CPU core to handle two instruction threads simultaneously.
questions.explanation: Hyper-Threading improves CPU efficiency through simultaneous multithreading.

questions.question: The bus connecting the CPU to memory for data transfer.
questions.explanation: FSB determines the speed of communication between CPU and RAM.

questions.question: ROM chip containing firmware for booting and hardware initialization.
questions.explanation: EEPROM stores BIOS or UEFI firmware that can be updated.

questions.question: Power management standard allowing the OS to control device power states.
questions.explanation: ACPI enables features like sleep mode and power management.

questions.question: Process of loading a small program that then loads the full operating system.
questions.explanation: Bootstrapping is the multi-stage boot process starting from firmware.

questions.question: The physical connection point on the motherboard for the CPU.
questions.explanation: CPU sockets vary by manufacturer and determine CPU compatibility.

questions.question: Memory controller managing communication between CPU and RAM.
questions.explanation: Modern CPUs have integrated memory controllers for faster access.

questions.question: Process of adjusting hardware settings beyond manufacturer specifications for better performance.
questions.explanation: Overclocking increases clock speeds but may reduce stability and lifespan.

questions.question: A user installs a 250 W GPU on a 400 W PSU and the PC shuts down under load; which PSU spec matters here?
questions.explanation: The PSU's wattage rating must exceed the total power draw of all components or the system shuts down under load.

questions.question: The three-stage cycle a CPU repeats for every instruction.
questions.explanation: The CPU fetches an instruction from memory, decodes it, then executes it, billions of times per second.

questions.question: Intel technology that raises CPU speed above base clock when extra performance is needed.
questions.explanation: Turbo Boost increases clock frequency dynamically within thermal and power limits.

questions.question: Power state that saves the session to disk so the PC can be fully powered off, unlike sleep.
questions.explanation: Hibernation writes RAM contents to a hibernation file on disk, using zero power while off.

questions.question: Material a technician applies between the CPU and heatsink to improve heat transfer.
questions.explanation: Thermal paste fills microscopic gaps between the CPU heat spreader and heatsink for better conductivity.

questions.question: A CPU is rated at 3.2 GHz. Roughly how many clock cycles does it complete in 5 seconds?
questions.explanation: 3.2 GHz means 3.2 billion cycles per second; multiplied by 5 seconds gives 16 billion cycles.

questions.question: A PC takes 40 seconds to reach the desktop from a hard drive but only 10 seconds after cloning the same data to an SSD. Which storage property, not capacity, explains the difference?
questions.explanation: SSDs have near-zero access times and far faster random reads, so scattered boot files load much quicker than from spinning platters.

questions.question: A user upgrades from 8 GB to 16 GB of RAM and heavy multitasking stops stuttering. Which disk-based memory technique had previously been overused, causing the slowdown?
questions.explanation: When RAM fills, the OS swaps memory pages to disk (paging); the extra RAM reduces this slow disk traffic.

questions.question: A game uses 100% of the CPU but only 40% of the GPU, capping frame rates. What is the common name for this performance imbalance?
questions.explanation: The slowest component limits the whole system; here the CPU bottleneck starves the GPU of work.

questions.question: A desktop boots to a black screen whenever a USB flash drive is left plugged in, but starts Windows normally without it. Which BIOS/UEFI setting should the technician adjust?
questions.explanation: The firmware is attempting to boot from USB first; moving the internal drive above USB in the boot order fixes it.
